speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your double vision and weakness, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and whether they seem to worsen as the day progresses?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest, along with eye movement issues, is very characteristic. Do you experience any difficulty with swallowing, speaking, or chewing, especially towards the end of the day?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To further narrow down the cause, I need to know if you have noticed any drooping of your eyelids or if you have had any recent thyroid problems.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you didn't mention whether you have eyelid drooping, which is a key sign. Do you experience any ptosis or drooping of your eyelids, particularly later in the day?

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand that the weakness fluctuates with activity and rest, which is a significant clue. To confirm my suspicion, I need to rule out other causes, so I will request a specific blood test and an imaging study.

REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_Test
REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); CT_Chest: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of acetylcholine receptor antibodies combined with your characteristic fluctuating muscle weakness and double vision confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
